name: CapCut Perspective Freeze Text Stack
use_when: Words should appear angled, dimensional, or fitted into a scene environment.
A short title or thumbnail-style composition needs staggered perspective words.
The editor wants text to fit between objects, ropes, architecture, slopes, or diagonal negative space.
B-cam footage or landscapes have clear planes where words can feel placed inside the scene.
avoid_when: The phrase is long or needs plain caption readability.
The chosen perspective frame makes the word harder to read.
The blend mode makes text disappear into the background.
The shot has no clear geometry or negative space for the perspective angle.

timeline_pattern.pattern: text_layer -> compound -> apply_perspective_animation -> choose_frame -> compound_again -> freeze_frame -> delete_unused_animation_tail -> repeat_words -> stagger_freezes -> group_reposition_scale -> optional_blend_mode
timeline_pattern.freeze_rule: Freeze only the perspective frame that reads best, then delete the pre-freeze animation tail if the final composition should be static.
timeline_pattern.template_rule: Keep one reusable compound text layer aside for future words.
timeline_pattern.size_rule: If the perspective animation shrinks the text, reopen the compound and resize the internal text layer instead of scaling a low-quality result.
timeline_pattern.environment_rule: Fit the angled words into real scene geometry or negative space rather than placing them randomly.
timeline_pattern.landscape_rule: For slopes, walls, or distant planes, rotate and scale each frozen word to match the plane direction and apparent distance.

motion.rule: The finished stack can be static or staggered; stagger only if the reading order remains clear.

keyframe_values.perspective_source: CapCut Combo animation Flip 6 can be used to find several angled text frames.
keyframe_values.font_spacing_start: Clean bold sans text with slight tightening, such as Character -1 on large words, can help the perspective word feel premium when readability holds.
keyframe_values.stagger: Offset frozen words slightly so each one appears in reading order.
keyframe_values.group_transform: After freezing words, select and resize/reposition the group together to preserve spacing.
keyframe_values.distance_scaling: Reduce word size when placing text on farther scene planes so the perspective feels motivated.

sound.rule: Use subtle ticks or pops only on staggered word entrances and keep them below speech.

captions.rule: Suppress ordinary captions if they duplicate the perspective words and clutter the same region.

color.rule: Blend modes such as Overlay can integrate text into footage only when letter edges remain readable.

implementation.ffmpeg: Pre-render perspective text images or use perspective transform filters, then overlay staggered PNG/text layers and optionally apply blend modes.
implementation.remotion: Model each word as a transformed layer with rotate/skew/perspective tokens, staggered start frames, blendMode, and group transform metadata.
implementation.blender: Use 3D text or planes with camera perspective, freeze by using still frames or static keyframes, and composite into the scene.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create a text layer, compound it, apply Combo > Flip 6 or another perspective animation, choose the best angled frame, reopen the compound if internal text size needs adjustment, compound again, freeze frame, delete unused animation before/after the freeze, repeat for other words, stagger the freeze frames, then group reposition/scale or rotate to match scene planes. Use Overlay blend only if readability holds.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics or nested text with Basic 3D/corner pin/perspective transforms, export stills or freeze frames, stagger layers, and use blend modes carefully.

common_mistakes: Choosing a cool perspective frame where the word is too skewed to read.
Forgetting to remove unused animated compound sections before the freeze frame.
Leaving no reusable source compound for future word changes.
Using Overlay blend until the text edge disappears.
Stacking perspective words without a clear reading order.
Using the same scale and rotation on foreground and distant scene planes.
qc: Can every frozen word be read at phone size?
Do the words fit scene geometry or intentional negative space?
Are unused animation tails removed before delivery?
Does any blend mode preserve edge contrast?
Is there one clear reading order through the staggered stack?
Do scene-attached words match the angle, scale, and distance of the plane they sit on?
